summary: Delivered on the appearance day of Lord Nityananda, this lecture first establishes why the Lord descends in every age to reintroduce dharma and why, in Kali-yuga, the prescribed process (yuga-dharma) is simply the congregational chanting of the Hare Krishna maha-mantra, which Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu received from his guru Ishvara Puri and gave to all. Indradyumna Swami identifies Nityananda as the first expansion of Krishna, non-different from Balarama (differing only in complexion), and as one of the five features of the Panca-tattva. He explains the unique glory of the Gaura-Nitai avatar: unlike Krishna and Rama, who allowed conditioned souls only to witness their pastimes, Chaitanya and Nityananda invite everyone onto the 'stage' to join the sankirtana, and Nityananda in particular is the supremely merciful one who went out to the masses to make people chant while Mahaprabhu preached to leaders such as Prakashananda Sarasvati and Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya. The swami narrates Nityananda's life: his 1473 appearance at Ekachakra to Hadai Pandita and Padmavati, his childhood enactment of the Ramayana, his leaving home at twelve with a wandering sannyasi (who carried a Murlidhara deity in which the mother saw her son's face), his initiation from Lakshmipati near Pandharpur, and his years wandering as a prema-intoxicated avadhuta before his ecstatic first reunion with Mahaprabhu at Navadvipa. Key pastimes are recounted to show his power and compassion: his roar that rendered the whole universe unconscious at Mahaprabhu's birth, the deliverance of the great sinners Jagai and Madhai (after which Mahaprabhu absorbed their sins and warned against criticizing any Vaishnava), his breaking of Mahaprabhu's sannyasa-danda, and his becoming a householder to demonstrate that grihasthas too can attain perfection. Throughout, the swami exhorts the audience to seize Kali-yuga's special opportunity by chanting sixteen rounds daily (citing a fifteen-year-old girl's example), avoiding offense to devotees, trusting the holy name to burn away all sin, and fearlessly going out to distribute prasadam and the holy name, closing with a 1970 letter of Srila Prabhupada on approaching the fallen at personal risk.
key_points: In each age the Lord gives a different process of self-realization; for Kali-yuga the yuga-dharma is nama-sankirtana, and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu established the Hare Krishna maha-mantra (received from Ishvara Puri) as the universal means of deliverance.

Nityananda is the first expansion of Krishna, identical to Balarama except in complexion, and one of the five features of the Panca-tattva; Gaura and Nitai are likened to the sun and moon that dissipate the darkness of ignorance.

The unique mercy of the Gaura-Nitai descent is that they draw conditioned souls directly into their pastimes through sankirtana, whereas in Krishna-lila and Rama-lila the conditioned souls could only witness the pastimes.

Nityananda is the embodiment of compassion and service who went to the masses to make everyone chant, illustrated by his deliverance of Jagai and Madhai and his bold, unconventional preaching alongside Haridasa Thakura.

Biographical arc: appearance at Ekachakra (1473), childhood Ramayana play, departure with a sannyasi at age twelve, initiation from Lakshmipati, wandering as a prema-mad avadhuta, and the ecstatic reunion with Mahaprabhu at Navadvipa.

Practical exhortations: chant sixteen rounds daily (the example of a fifteen-year-old girl), never criticize a Vaishnava (Mahaprabhu's warning tied to Jagai-Madhai's sins), trust the holy name to destroy all sinful reactions, and go out fearlessly to distribute the holy name and prasadam.

Ashrama teaching: Mahaprabhu had Nityananda marry to prove householders can also attain perfection; per Narottama dasa Thakura, whether renunciate or householder, anyone who sincerely serves the sankirtana movement is worthy of association.
references: Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi-lila 1.2 - 'I offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Chaitanya and Lord Nityananda, who are like the sun and the moon, arisen simultaneously on the horizon of Gauda to dissipate the darkness of ignorance and thus wonderfully bestow benediction upon all.' Quoted from Krishnadasa Kaviraja Goswami to state the mission of the two brothers.

Bhagavad-gita 7.3 - 'manushyanam sahasreshu kascid yatati siddhaye'; among many, hardly one strives for perfection and of those hardly one knows Krishna in truth (used to describe the spiritual decline of Dvapara-yuga).

Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.3.51 - 'kirtanad eva krishnasya mukta-sangah param vrajet'; Shukadeva Goswami tells Maharaja Pariksit that though Kali-yuga is 'an ocean of inauspiciousness,' the one good thing left is that by chanting Krishna's name one is freed and attains the goal.
Bhagavad-gita 18.66 - 'sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam sharanam vraja'; Krishna's parting instruction to fully surrender, cited as the teaching he left behind on departing the world.

Srimad-Bhagavatam, Venu-gita (10.21.5) - 'barhapidam nata-vara-vapuh karnayoh karnikaram...'; describes Krishna with a peacock-feather ornament, karnikara flowers on his ears, a golden-yellow garment and the Vaijayanti garland entering the Vrindavan forest as the greatest of dancers. Recited by Gadadhara Pandita to revive Chaitanya and Nityananda (the speaker cited it as Canto 10, Chapter 25, verse 5).

Narottama dasa Thakura - 'Brajendra-nandana yei, saci-suta hoilo sei, balarama hoilo nitai'; Krishna the prince of Vraja appeared as Chaitanya, and Balarama appeared as Nitai (cited as the sadhu/authority testifying to the brothers' identity).

Chaitanya Bhagavata (Vrindavana dasa Thakura) - glorifies Nityananda as tattva-sima (the very limit of the Absolute Truth), purna-shakti (the total potency of God), seva-vigraha (the embodiment of service), and murti-manta-krishna-prema (the embodiment of love of God); also 'He alone can see him whom Lord Chaitanya shows.'

Panca-tattva (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi-lila) - in Kali-yuga the Lord appears in five features: Chaitanya (the devotee), Nityananda (his expansion/prakasha), Advaita Acharya (the incarnation), Gadadhara (the internal potency, Srimati Radharani), and Srivasa Thakura (the marginal energy).

Srimad-Bhagavatam 6.3.19 - 'dharmam tu sakshad bhagavat-pranitam'; real religious principles are enacted directly by the Lord, paraphrased at the opening to explain why only Krishna can teach genuine dharma.

Adi Purana (quoted in Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya-lila) - Krishna states that one who claims to be His devotee is not truly His devotee, but one who is the devotee of His devotee is very dear to Him (cited when Padmavati serves the sadhu by giving her son).

Srila Prabhupada, letter dated January 27, 1970 - 'Nityananda Prabhu approached Jagai and Madhai at the risk of being personally injured and still he definitely delivered them. The world is full of Jagais and Madhais...'; read aloud to conclude, on fearlessly approaching the fallen and accepting hardship as the greatest penance in spiritual advancement.
stories: Nityananda's roar — sensing Mahaprabhu's birth by mystic power, he roared so loud the entire universe fell unconscious.
The childhood Ramayana play — as a boy Nitai played Lakshmana, 'struck' by a flower and revived with a sweet from his mother's cabinet.
The sannyasi asks for the boy — a wandering sannyasi begs milk, then asks for twelve-year-old Nitai; his mother sees Nitai's face in the Murlidhara deity and consents.
First reunion at Navadvipa — Gaura and Nitai run together, embrace in a flood of tears and fall unconscious, revived by Bhagavatam verses and kirtan.
The thief who stole my heart — Mahaprabhu tells Nityananda he searched the whole world and at last found the thief who stole his heart.
Nitai the wild preacher — threatening to break people's furniture until they chant, and swimming among crocodiles, making him Haridasa's most troublesome sankirtana partner.
Jagai and Madhai delivered — after the brothers show remorse, Mahaprabhu embraces them, absorbs their sins and turns black, warning never to criticize a Vaishnava.
Breaking the sannyasa-danda — Nitai snaps Mahaprabhu's staff into pieces and throws it in the river, which the acharyas explain released the flood of Krishna-prema.
quotes: I searched the whole world over but could not find you, now I have found the thief who has stolen my heart, now I will never let you go.
He alone can see him who Lord Chaitanya shows.
Don't be wall flowers, be lotus flowers.
chant Hare Krishna and your life will be sublime.
